commenti.body:
definitely an opus of one of the masters and originators of extreme cinema. his other films besides the big two (this and possession) don’t get enough love either. Hard to overstate the impact and influence possession had so it’s pretty cool to think about what this could have been for sci-fi as a finished product.

i was lucky enough to see a print of this in theaters a couple of years back and it was a very mesmerizing experience. It just feels like such a successful piece of art despite it being literally incomplete—he captures the energy he was going for perfectly.

one of my favorites

Well said! One of the greatest films of all time and an absolute masterpiece!

Only haven't gotten around to seeing Hard to Be A God yet but I'm dying to.

And also, pretty much the whole of Zulawskis filmography is worth checking out.

Fascinating film! It's like a mix of Tarkovsky and Jodorowsky, and with the accompanying documentary Escape to the Silver Globe it has the feeling of a Polish Dune, sitting between the unrealized or not fully realized projects in the past. The added footage is not a bad audition and provides some safe space in the madness and some clarity in the story. I really recommend the documentary to get an idea about what was going on really and what inspired Julawsky.

My friend showed my vanilla filmwatching ass this movie and I swear to god, I literally freaked out at the end. I was stirred beyond any previous film. I was pissed, and confused, and discombobulated.

Great guy.

I watch much better movies now, for what it's worth. But the above is what happens when you break a film baby.

It had to happen.
I'm surprised you made it all the way through given that context tbh

It's incredibly overrated. The costumes are absolutely brilliant but other than that I cannot see it as anything but pretentious. It has some of the worst dialogue I have ever seen in a movie. In film writing 101, they teach you not to have your characters say out loud how they feel, well that's 80% of the dialogue in this movie. The characters just constantly \*scream\* pseudo-philosophy throughout the entire thing. It's not fun. Why are they screaming too? Do you ever just go for a swim and then scream out the 8 noble paths with the tone of begging for your life?

I cannot help not compare this movie to Dune (the book) as I feel like they have much in common both superfically and thematically, but Dune actually succeeds. Spoilers for Dune: It also claims that religon is man-made tool for control, but this is shown to you. At no point does any of the characters go into the desert to scream about how religion is a tool to control the weak.

So fucking good. My buddy had it on some weird file and we hung out and watched it. When it comes to Kulawski, I had only seen Possession, which was sick, but OTSG blew me away and became one of my top 100.

Regarding the dialogue, that's just par for the course for a lot of Russian/Eastern European films from that time. I assume the concept of filmmaking developed differently there and this is the end result. Once I've accepted this, I can just experience the film for what it is.

> In film writing 101, they teach you not to have your characters say out loud how they feel, well that's 80% of the dialogue in this movie. The characters just constantly *scream* pseudo-philosophy throughout the entire thing. It's not fun. Why are they screaming too? Do you ever just go for a swim and then scream out the 8 noble paths with the tone of begging for your life?

You've just sold me on watching it. I love that sort of stuff. That Film 101 viewpoint is just a temporary middlebrow fashion and not some eternal verity of drama. I love ancient Greek drama and Milton where characters philosophize grandly.

Of course, it may be done badly in this case (I'll have to watch it to find out) but I'm not against it in principal.

Film writing 101 level understanding/appreciation is going to get you film 101 level films. 

This is like holding Bresson's or Kurosawa's actor's in a bad light because they are trying to do something different with dialog and the idea of performance in their films.

I also thought this one was just insufferable. It has to be one of the most unenjoyable movie experiences of my entire life, and I actually really enjoy really out there shit. The philosophical rambling was intolerable.

I think the first 20 minutes is a little slow, and then it gets insane. Just when its gaining traction and making sense, it completely flips the script and I think falls a little short of how great it was heading to. I think it was a good movie, not necassarily the most enjoyable movies to watch, but I dont think it was meant to be a easy viewing. That being said I think where it maybe could have been improved was in the destroyed scenes that are replaced with exposition.

It's a bad movie that tries to look good by laying out all the pseudo philosophy by the dialogue, everyone in the movie is a philosopher, of it was made today people will call it pretentious. This is one of those movies that benefits from the fact that they're old and non English. The director should have written an essay telling of his pseudo philosophical bs instead of making the movie.
